adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/sentry/uptime/consumers/test_results_consumer.py:1922 — assert len(committed_offsets) == 0 or test_partition not in committed_offsets` is a weak/racy assertion whose two disjuncts are redundant given only one partition is used, and its outcome depends on whether the 1-second `_commit_loop` tick (queue_consumer.py:276) has fired yet by the time the test's own poll loop exits, so the test can pass for the wrong reason (loop simply hasn't ticked) rather than confirming the intended guarantee.

adjudication.rationale: The cited assertion in `test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling` (`assert len(committed_offsets) == 0 or test_partition not in committed_offsets`) is indeed weak/racy given the diff: `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy` commits on a background thread that ticks once per second (`self.shutdown_event.wait(1.0)` in `_commit_loop`), while the test’s polling loop can exit as soon as `stats["total_items"] == 0` and `call_count >= 2`, potentially well before the 1-second commit tick fires. In that case `committed_offsets` can remain empty simply because the commit loop hasn’t run yet, not because offsets won’t be committed. Also, within this test only `test_partition` is used/updated, so `len(committed_offsets) == 0` and `test_partition not in committed_offsets` are effectively equivalent, making the disjunction redundant.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py:335 — SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()/terminate() call self.queue_pool.shutdown() on the FixedQueuePool that ResultsStrategyFactory creates once and reuses across every create_with_partitions() call (i.e. every rebalance, see result_consumer.py:133 and :254); after the first rebalance the shared pool's workers/queues are permanently dead, so subsequent submit() calls hit queue.put() raising queue.ShutDown, which is caught by SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit()'s except-block and immediately add_offset+complete_offset the message (queue_consumer.py:317-325), silently marking messages as committed without ever running result_processor on them

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows ResultsStrategyFactory creates `self.queue_pool = FixedQueuePool(...)` once in `__init__` when `mode == "thread-queue-parallel"` (result_consumer.py) and then `create_thread_queue_parallel_worker` passes that same `self.queue_pool` into each new `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy`. But `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()` and `terminate()` both call `self.queue_pool.shutdown()` (queue_consumer.py), which permanently shuts down the pool’s worker threads and calls `q.shutdown(...)` on each queue. Since the factory does not recreate the pool on subsequent `create_with_partitions` calls (it reuses the existing `self.queue_pool` unless `factory.shutdown()` is called), a later strategy will use a dead pool; `FixedQueuePool.submit()` will then hit `work_queue.put(...)` on a shutdown queue (raising `queue.ShutDown`), which is caught by `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit()`’s broad `except Exception:` and results in `add_offset`+`complete_offset`, allowing offsets to be committed without processing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py:231 — FixedQueuePool.shutdown()` (a method) coexists with `OrderedQueueWorker.shutdown` (a bool attribute, queue_consumer.py:125) and an unrelated `ResultsStrategyFactory.shutdown()` (result_consumer.py:180), making "shutdown" mean three different things across closely-related classes and hurting readability

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `FixedQueuePool.shutdown(self) -> None` (queue_consumer.py) while `OrderedQueueWorker` has a `shutdown` boolean attribute used as a loop condition (`while not self.shutdown:`) and `ResultsStrategyFactory` already defines a `shutdown(self) -> None` method (result_consumer.py). These closely related classes now use the same word to mean different concepts (method vs flag vs factory lifecycle method), which is a concrete readability/maintainability concern visible in the diff, though not a functional defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py:31 — WorkItem.message` is stored on every work item (set at queue_consumer.py:312) but never read anywhere in queue_consumer.py or result_consumer.py, retaining a full Kafka `Message` reference per queued item for no apparent benefit

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `WorkItem` includes a `message: Message[...]` field (new in `queue_consumer.py`), and `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit` populates it when constructing `WorkItem` (around the shown creation at `work_item = WorkItem(..., message=message)`). However, the worker (`OrderedQueueWorker.run`) only uses `work_item.result`, `work_item.partition`, and `work_item.offset`, and the offset tracking/commit logic also only uses partition/offset. There is no read of `work_item.message` anywhere in `queue_consumer.py` or the modified `result_consumer.py`, so this retains a full Kafka `Message` per queued item without an apparent use, which is a concrete, diff-grounded memory/perf concern rather than a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/sentry/uptime/consumers/test_results_consumer.py:1922 — assert len(committed_offsets) == 0 or test_partition not in committed_offsets` is nearly tautological and can't distinguish "errors correctly handled" from "commit thread just hasn't ticked yet"

adjudication.rationale: In `test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling`, the assertion `len(committed_offsets) == 0 or test_partition not in committed_offsets` is logically redundant (if the dict is empty, the partition cannot be present) and, more importantly, the test can pass simply because the background commit thread in `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy._commit_loop` hasn’t run yet. The test only waits for queue drain and processor calls, not for an absence/presence of commits, so it does not reliably validate the stated behavior (“errors … don’t block offset commits for other messages”). This is a diff-grounded test weakness rather than a direct functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/sentry/uptime/consumers/test_results_consumer.py:2005 — test_thread_queue_parallel_graceful_shutdown only asserts `factory.queue_pool is None`, never verifying the 5 submitted results were actually processed (or intentionally dropped) before shutdown completes

adjudication.rationale: In `test_thread_queue_parallel_graceful_shutdown`, the test submits 5 results and immediately calls `factory.shutdown()`, then only asserts `factory.queue_pool is None` (see added test near the end of the diff). It does not assert that the queued work was processed before shutdown, nor that shutdown intentionally drops in-flight items. Given the new shutdown behavior (`ResultsStrategyFactory.shutdown` calls `self.queue_pool.shutdown()` and then sets `queue_pool = None`), this test currently validates only that the reference is cleared, not that shutdown is graceful with respect to processing/offset completion.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/sentry/uptime/consumers/test_results_consumer.py:1859 — test_thread_queue_parallel_offset_commit polls unrelated `queue_pool` stats with a hard 2s cap (20*0.1s) against the commit loop's hardcoded 1s timer, leaving thin margin and risking flakiness on slow CI, unlike the explicit `commit_event.wait()` used for the same scenario in test_queue_consumer.py

adjudication.rationale: In `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy._commit_loop` the commit thread waits on `shutdown_event.wait(1.0)` before attempting commits, i.e. commits can be delayed up to ~1s. In `tests/sentry/uptime/consumers/test_results_consumer.py` `test_thread_queue_parallel_offset_commit` uses a polling loop capped at `max_wait = 20` with `time.sleep(0.1)` (~2s total) and checks `stats["total_items"] == 0 and len(committed_offsets) > 0` rather than waiting on an explicit commit signal. This creates a thin timing margin on slow CI and is a concrete test-flakiness risk, especially compared to `tests/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/test_queue_consumer.py` which uses `commit_event.wait(...)` to synchronize commits.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/sentry/uptime/consumers/test_results_consumer.py:1960 — test_thread_queue_parallel_offset_gaps has the same 2s-poll-vs-1s-commit-timer race as test_thread_queue_parallel_offset_commit instead of waiting on an explicit commit signal

adjudication.rationale: In the new uptime tests, `test_thread_queue_parallel_offset_gaps` (and similarly `test_thread_queue_parallel_offset_commit`) polls for at most ~2s (`max_wait=20` with `time.sleep(0.1)`) for `all_commits`/`committed_offsets` to be populated. But the production implementation’s commit loop in `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy._commit_loop` wakes on a fixed 1.0s interval (`shutdown_event.wait(1.0)`) and only then computes/commits committable offsets. Since processing can finish quickly (queues empty) but the next commit tick can be delayed by scheduling/CI load, this test can race/flap without an explicit “commit happened” signal (unlike `tests/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/test_queue_consumer.py` which uses `commit_event`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/test_queue_consumer.py:22 — OffsetTracker (TestOffsetTracker) has no concurrent/multi-threaded stress test for `_get_partition_lock`'s get-then-setdefault pattern despite it being the core correctness guarantee of the whole feature

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new concurrent offset-tracking logic in `OffsetTracker`, including `_get_partition_lock` which uses a get-then-`setdefault` pattern on `self.partition_locks` without any global synchronization. The added tests in `tests/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/test_queue_consumer.py` (e.g., `TestOffsetTracker`) only exercise single-threaded behavior and do not stress `_get_partition_lock` under concurrent access, even though the class is explicitly documented as “Thread-safe for concurrent access with per-partition locks.” This is a specific, diff-grounded missing-test concern rather than a verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/sentry/uptime/consumers/test_results_consumer.py:2017 — ProcessResultThreadQueueParallelKafkaTest is gated by `requires_kafka` and is likely skipped in normal CI runs, giving false confidence that the real-Kafka offset-commit guarantee is covered

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `ProcessResultThreadQueueParallelKafkaTest` with `pytestmark = [requires_kafka]`, which explicitly gates the real-Kafka integration test (`test_thread_queue_parallel_kafka_offset_commit`) behind a skip condition. From the diff alone we can verify it will not run unless the CI environment satisfies `requires_kafka`, so relying on it for coverage in “normal” runs could indeed give false confidence about Kafka-level offset commit behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/sentry/uptime/consumers/test_results_consumer.py:1891 — error handling for thread-queue-parallel mode is only exercised via a mocked exception injection; no test covers a real exception raised from result_processor's actual DB/model code path (partial batch failure / thread crash)

adjudication.rationale: In the new uptime thread-queue-parallel tests, error handling is indeed only exercised by mocking the result processor call and injecting an exception (e.g., `test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling` uses `mock.patch.object(type(factory.result_processor), "__call__")` with `side_effect = [Exception(...), None]`). All the added thread-queue-parallel uptime tests similarly patch the processor rather than running the real `ResultProcessor` implementation that would hit DB/model code. Given the new threaded worker/commit logic (`OrderedQueueWorker.run` catches `Exception` and continues), a more realistic integration-style test could be warranted to cover failures in the actual processing path.
